title: Run a script file
summary: `lua script.lua args...`: the standalone interpreter creates a state, compiles the file into a main closure, then calls it in protected mode until the VM returns. Compilation and the call mechanics are detailed in the drill-down flows.

title: Interpreter entry point
notes: Creates the state with `luaL_newstate` and **stops the GC** while the state is being built. Everything else runs inside `pmain` so that errors (even out-of-memory while opening libraries) are caught by `lua_pcall` instead of aborting the process.

title: Protected main: options, libs, script
notes: Receives `argc`/`argv` as a Lua integer and a light userdata. Order matters: parse options → `luaL_openlibs` → build the global `arg` table → restart GC in **generational** mode → `LUA_INIT` → `-e`/`-l` → script → REPL. Returns `true` on the stack to tell `main` no error was reported.

title: Load and run the script
notes: `-` as script name means stdin (unless preceded by `--`). Script arguments are pushed from `arg[1..n]`, and the chunk is called with `LUA_MULTRET`.

title: Open file and feed it to the loader
notes:
Reached through the macro `luaL_loadfile(L,f)` = `luaL_loadfilex(L,f,NULL)` (mode `NULL` accepts text and binary).

- Chunk name is `"@filename"` (the `@` marks a file in error messages).
- A first line starting with `#` (shebang) is skipped but replaced by `\n` so line numbers stay right.
- If the first byte is `LUA_SIGNATURE[0]` (`\x1b`) the file is reopened in binary mode.
- The file is closed even on error; read errors override the load status.

title: File reader callback
notes: `lua_Reader` for files: first returns the bytes pre-read by `luaL_loadfilex`, then `fread`s blocks of `BUFSIZ`. Checks `feof` before reading so an interactive stdin is not asked for more input after EOF.

title: Load a chunk (public API)
notes: Wraps the reader in a `ZIO` stream. On success the new closure is on the stack top and its **first upvalue is set to the global table** — that upvalue is `_ENV`, which is how free names in the chunk become globals.

title: Parse in protected mode
notes: Increments the non-yieldable counter (`incnny`): parsing can never yield. Owns the scanner buffer and the parser's dynamic arrays (`actvar`, `gt`, `label`) and frees them whether or not parsing failed.

title: Run a C function with error recovery
notes: Calls `luaD_rawrunprotected`, i.e. `setjmp`/`longjmp` (or C++ `try`/`catch` when compiled as C++). On error it restores `L->ci` and `allowhook`, closes pending to-be-closed variables and upvalues, places the error object at `old_top` and shrinks an overflowed stack back.

title: Choose text or binary loader
notes: Peeks the first byte: `\x1b` → `luaU_undump` (precompiled chunk), otherwise the source parser. `checkmode` raises `LUA_ERRSYNTAX` if the load mode forbids the chunk type. Finally `luaF_initupvals` gives the closure fresh (closed) upvalues.

title: Compile source to a main closure
Call chunk with traceback handler
notes: Inserts `msghandler` below the function so runtime errors get a traceback, and installs a `SIGINT` handler for the duration of the call: Ctrl-C sets a hook that raises an error at the next instruction instead of killing the process.

title: Protected call (public API)
notes: `lua_pcall` is a macro for `lua_pcallk(L,n,r,f,0,NULL)`. Without a continuation (or when not yieldable) it does a conventional `luaD_pcall`; with one, the call is already protected by `lua_resume`, so it just calls `luaD_call` and records recovery info in the `CallInfo`.

title: Call a function from C
notes: Bumps `L->nCcalls` (C-stack depth; `luaD_callnoyield` also marks the call non-yieldable) and errors with "C stack overflow" past `LUAI_MAXCCALLS`. For a Lua function, the new `CallInfo` is marked `CIST_FRESH` so `luaV_execute` knows to return to C when it finishes.

title: Interpret bytecode
notes: The main interpreter loop. Lua-to-Lua calls inside the script do **not** recurse in C: they reuse this same C frame (see the call-function flow).

label: run everything under lua_pcall
notes: `pmain` is pushed as a C function and invoked through `lua_pcall` → … → `precallC`.

label: compile file, don't run it yet
ZIO needs bytes
notes: `zgetc` → `luaZ_fill` calls the reader whenever the stream buffer is empty; this keeps happening while the lexer reads.

label: LUA_OK, main closure on stack
notes: On a syntax error the status is `LUA_ERRSYNTAX` and the message is on the stack instead; `report` prints it and the script is never run.

label: Lua function: run fresh VM frame
notes: `luaD_precall` builds the frame first; see the call-function flow.
